high|Art. 10.text: Training, validation and testing data sets must meet quality criteria — relevance, representativeness, freedom from errors and completeness. Documentation of the data sets is required.
high|Art. 10.title: Data and data governance

high|Art. 11.text: Complete technical documentation in accordance with Annex IV to the EU AI Act is required before the system is placed on the market or put into service. The documentation must be kept up to date throughout the system's lifecycle.
high|Art. 11.title: Technical documentation

high|Art. 13.text: The AI system must ensure operational transparency. Users must be informed that they are interacting with an AI system and understand how it works to the extent necessary for oversight.
high|Art. 13.title: Transparency and provision of information

high|Art. 14.text: Measures are in place enabling natural persons to understand, monitor and intervene in the operation of the AI system. It must be possible to stop or reverse any decision made by the system.
high|Art. 14.title: Human oversight

high|Art. 15.text: The system must achieve an appropriate level of accuracy throughout its lifecycle. Testing of resilience to errors, attacks and unexpected inputs is required.
high|Art. 15.title: Accuracy and robustness

high|Art. 17.text: The provider puts in place a quality management system comprising policies, procedures and instructions to ensure compliance with the EU AI Act.
high|Art. 17.title: Quality management system

high|Art. 26 ust. 2.text: The deployer of a high-risk AI system must assign human oversight to natural persons who have the necessary competence, training and authority, as well as the necessary support.
high|Art. 26 ust. 2.title: Human oversight assigned to a competent person

high|Art. 26 ust. 5.text: The deployer must monitor the operation of the system on the basis of the instructions for use and inform the provider and, where relevant, the market surveillance authority of any identified risk or serious incident.
high|Art. 26 ust. 5.title: Monitoring of operation and informing the provider

high|Art. 26 ust. 6.text: The deployer must keep the logs automatically generated by the system for a period appropriate to the intended purpose of the system, of at least six months, unless provided otherwise in applicable Union or national law.
high|Art. 26 ust. 6.title: Retention of automatically generated logs

high|Art. 26 ust. 8.text: A deployer that is a public authority must comply with the registration obligations referred to in Art. 49 and, before putting the system into service, verify that it is registered in the EU database.
high|Art. 26 ust. 8.title: Verification of registration in the EU database

high|Art. 27.text: Before deploying a high-risk AI system referred to in Annex III, point 5(b) or (c) (creditworthiness assessment, insurance risk), or where the deployer is a body governed by public law or a private entity providing public services, the deployer must perform a fundamental rights impact assessment: a description of the processes in which the system will be used, the period and frequency of use, the categories of persons affected, the risks of harm to those persons, and the human oversight measures and complaint mechanisms.
high|Art. 27.title: Fundamental rights impact assessment (FRIA)

high|Art. 43.text: High-risk AI systems listed in Annex III must undergo a conformity assessment (internal control or involving a notified body) before being placed on the market or put into service.
high|Art. 43.title: Conformity assessment

high|Art. 49.text: High-risk AI systems must be registered in the EU database before being placed on the market or put into service.
high|Art. 49.title: Registration in the EU database

high|Art. 9.text: A high-risk agent requires a documented risk management system throughout its entire lifecycle. Identification, analysis and evaluation of risks and the adoption of risk management measures are required.
high|Art. 9.title: Risk management system

limited|Art. 50 ust. 1.text: Systems intended to interact with natural persons must inform the user in a clear, distinguishable and timely manner that they are interacting with an automated system, unless this is obvious.
limited|Art. 50 ust. 1.title: Obligation to disclose the use of AI

limited|Art. 50 ust. 4.text: AI-generated text, audio and video content must be marked in a machine-readable format as artificially generated.
limited|Art. 50 ust. 4.title: Marking of AI-generated content

minimal|Preambuła 46.text: No mandatory legal requirements apply to minimal-risk systems. The voluntary application of codes of conduct and general principles of trustworthy AI (transparency, fairness, safety) is recommended.
minimal|Preambuła 46.title: Voluntary codes of conduct

unacceptable|Art. 5.text: The AI practices listed in Art. 5 are strictly prohibited in the EU. It must be verified that the system does not fall into any of the prohibited categories (subliminal manipulation, social scoring, real-time biometric identification).
unacceptable|Art. 5.title: Absolute prohibition
